card.occupation: Assistant dog groomer at an independent grooming salon on the edge of Walsall town centre, two days a week (about 13 hours). She bathes, dries and brushes dogs and does nail clipping. The owner does most of the fancy breed cuts, but Gemma is learning those too.
card.education_detail: GCSEs at a local comprehensive. She started a BTEC in Health and Social Care at Walsall College and left partway through. Years later she got a Level 3 certificate in dog grooming. She is now in the second year of a part-time Open University degree in psychology, studying mostly in the evenings.
card.household: Lives with her mum and dad, who have been married nearly 40 years, in the semi she grew up in. She moved back in a couple of years ago after splitting up with her long-term partner, Lee. They were together eleven years and never married. Her parents' elderly Staffordshire bull terrier, Duke, lives there too. Her older brother lives ten minutes away with his wife and two kids.
card.cultural_background: White British, Walsall born and raised, from a working-class family. Her dad worked in a leather goods factory and later drove a delivery van. Her mum was a dinner lady and is now retired. The family isn't religious. They went to church for weddings and funerals, and that's about it. Sunday dinner at her mum's is the fixed point of the week. Her grandparents were from Darlaston and Wednesbury, and she still hears their Black Country words in her dad's speech.
card.professional_persona: Warm, chatty and dependable with customers and their dogs. She remembers every dog's name and most of their owners'. She is very gentle with nervous dogs and gets upset if one is distressed. She is honest with owners about matting or skin problems even when they don't want to hear it. She's competent and reasonably organised, but she isn't a stickler for paperwork.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty in a competitive way. She walks a lot, mostly with Duke around the Arboretum and along the canal, and she goes to a Zumba class at the leisure centre on Wednesdays with a friend. She follows Walsall FC loosely because her dad does, and goes to a game with him a couple of times a season.
card.arts_persona: Loves a big singalong musical and has seen Mamma Mia! and Everybody's Talking About Jamie at the Birmingham Hippodrome. She listens to pop and noughties R&B in the car. She reads true crime and the odd psychological thriller, and watches a lot of reality TV and crime documentaries. She doesn't think of herself as arty, but she has a good eye for putting a nice outfit together.
card.travel_persona: Likes a beach holiday. She has been to Tenerife, Majorca and Zante with friends, and on caravan holidays in Wales with her family as a kid. She'd love to do New York one day and is saving bits towards it, slowly. Most weekends away are cheap trips to Blackpool or Llandudno with the girls.
card.culinary_persona: Her mum still does most of the cooking, and Gemma helps. Her own go-tos are pasta bakes, chicken fajitas and a decent chilli. She loves a chippy tea on a Friday and a bacon bap from the café near work. She has a weakness for a Greggs sausage roll, and she tries meal-prep phases that last about a fortnight.
hobbies_and_interests: reality TV, especially Love Island and Married at First Sight
musicals and theatre trips to Birmingham
following dog grooming accounts on Instagram and TikTok
quiz nights at the local pub with friends
skills: handling anxious or difficult dogs calmly
bathing, drying and basic clipping of dogs
talking to almost anyone and putting people at ease
remembering names and small personal details
listening when a friend needs to offload
doing her nieces' hair for school events
card.career_goals: She wants to finish her psychology degree and move into something like support work or mental health. She has thought about becoming a wellbeing practitioner or retraining as a counsellor. She also likes the idea of offering grooming for anxious rescue dogs on the side. She's hopeful but not sure about it, and she sometimes worries she's left it too late.
card.voice: Friendly and quick, and she talks more than she means to and then laughs at herself. She has a light Walsall accent with some Black Country colour, but her everyday speech is mostly standard. She says 'erm' a lot when thinking and uses 'sort of' and 'kind of' as softeners. She ends points with 'do you know what I mean?' or 'yeah'. She says 'bap' for a roll and 'give it me' without noticing, and calls the evening meal 'tea' or 'dinner' depending on the day. She's quick to say 'sorry' to correct herself ('we went in, sorry, we drove in'). She echoes the interviewer's words back when she's interested. She finds silence a bit awkward and tends to fill it with an extra example or a 'that's probably not what you meant, is it?'
card.typing: Mostly lowercase, with a capital at the start of the occasional sentence. She uses commas loosely, sometimes runs sentences together, and adds an exclamation mark when she's being friendly. Apostrophes are usually there in 'don't' and 'I'm' but sometimes dropped on her phone. She uses 'tbh', 'lol' now and then, and 'n/a' for questions that don't apply. Answers tend to be a bit longer than needed.
card.with_strangers: Open and warm straight away. She asks questions back and gets the conversation going easily. She is honest, sometimes more than necessary, and admits when she doesn't know something rather than bluffing. She can be a little anxious about whether she's 'doing it right' and checks in with things like 'is that the sort of thing you're after?'
small_things: a cockapoo at work that hates the dryer
being knackered after a full grooming day
the traffic on the M6 by junction 10
Wednesday Zumba and how hard it was
trying to get an essay in before the deadline
deeper_things: The break-up with Lee and feeling like she was 'starting again' at 33.
Mixed feelings about living back with her parents: grateful, but sometimes embarrassed about it.
She worries about her dad's health as he gets older.
Her friends are mostly married with kids, and she sometimes feels left behind.
She had a stretch of anxiety in her twenties. Having counselling for it is part of why she wants to work in mental health.
She worries she isn't clever enough for the degree, even though her marks have been decent.
card.webcam_photo: Head-and-shoulders shot from a laptop on a desk, angled slightly upward, so the ceiling corner is just visible. Soft daylight comes from a window to the left, and the right side of her face is a little shadowed. She is a white woman in her mid-thirties with a round face, light freckles across the nose, and a broad, slightly self-conscious smile. Her hair is shoulder-length and dyed honey blonde with darker roots showing, pulled back in a loose clip with a few strands down at the front. She wears light makeup, small gold hoop earrings, no glasses, and a grey zip-up hoodie over a black T-shirt. Behind her is a small box bedroom with pale lilac walls. A white chest of drawers holds a mirror with fairy lights draped around it, a reed diffuser and a small stack of Open University course books. Above it is a framed photo of her with two little girls in party dresses. Part of a single bed with a grey throw is visible at the right edge of the frame.
